title: Telemetry Resurfacer with safety policies and resume tokens
creator: Leah Park
description: Build a resilient "resurfacer" service that performs tenant-scoped replays/backfills of late-arriving console telemetry while enforcing safety policies and providing resumable execution. The tool must produce dry-run reprocess plans, estimate cost & duration, and allow canary replays with automatic quarantine of suspect partitions. Design goals: idempotent application, visibility in Console, tenant-prioritized ordering, and minimal blast radius for large backfills.
acceptance_criteria: Resurfacer can generate a non-destructive dry-run plan that enumerates affected tenants, events, and estimated compute cost.
Replay jobs are resumable via per-tenant resume tokens and checkpointed watermarks; safe-window boundaries are respected to avoid interfering with live ingestion.
Integration tests cover idempotency: reapplying the same replay plan does not produce duplicate telemetry in downstream aggregates.
Console shows live progress for each job, including bytes processed, estimated ETA, cost burn rate, and quarantine alerts.
Automatic quarantine is triggered when schema mismatch, high error-rate, or checksum drift exceeds configured thresholds; quarantine produces a diagnostic bundle and blocks destructive writes.
Job-level throttles and tenant-priority queueing prevent noisy replays from overwhelming production RPC and ingestion pathways.
tasks: Design safe-window algorithm and watermark heuristics (Leah)
Implement resume token format and checkpointing API (Marco)
Dry-run planner: cost estimator and changed-row enumerator (backend)
Quarantine flow and diagnostic bundle creator
Console UI hooks for job visualization and controls
E2E tests: idempotency, failure recovery, quarantine triggers
Run a canary rehearsal on staging tenant with representative load
comments: 2025-02-10 Leah Park: Initial ticket. Spike completed: evaluated three approaches for safe-windowing — fixed-time windows, event-timestamp heuristics, and hybrid watermarking. Hybrid looks promising because it balances late-arrival tolerance vs. replay scope.

2025-02-14 Marco Gutierrez: Prototype checkpoint format posted to GH: redwood-inference/telemetry-resurfacer#8. Using compact resume token that encodes (tenant_id, partition, seq_highwater, schema_version). Tokens are opaque but decodable by the service.

2025-02-20 Leah Park: Trade-offs discussion in design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ANALYTICS/Telemetry+Resurfacer. Key decision: make dry-run the default for any >10k-event tenant replays to reduce accidental writes. Also agreed to compute cost estimate by sampling hourly throughput and applying quantiles to forecast CPU/GPU time.

2025-02-24 Marco Gutierrez: Implemented preliminary dry-run planner; it returns a JSON plan and estimated cost. Submitted PR for planner core: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-resurfacer/pull/17 — awaiting backend review.

2025-02-26 SRE (Anita Rao): Concern: long-running replays may interfere with autoscaler signals. Proposal: surface a per-job 'scale budget' that the controller honors; jobs above budget are throttled or rescheduled to off-peak windows.
2025-03-01 Leah Park: Added acceptance criteria for quarantine diagnostic bundle and console visibility. Decided to require canary runs for any replay touching >5% of active tenants.

2025-03-01 Marco Gutierrez: Note: implemented checkpointing to write resume tokens to durable store (DynamoDB), schema migration aware. Integration tests in CI failing on a corner case — schema-version drift when event schema changes mid-run; blocking fix in progress (ENG-412579 will track schema drift handler).
implementation_notes: Idempotency: use at-least-once ingestion but dedupe downstream by (tenant, event_origin_id) with a monotonic sequence check when available.
Checkpointing cadence: commit resume tokens after every 5k events or 30s, whichever comes first, to bound rework on failure.
Quarantine criteria: schema mismatch rate > 2% OR write error rate > 0.5% over a sliding 5m window triggers quarantine for that partition.
Cost model: sample 1% of events to build per-tenant cost profile, then apply multiplier for heavy queries (high sequence lengths).
Operational safety: default dry-run for large tenants, canaries for cross-tenant replays, and operator override guarded by 2-person approval for destructive runs.
